patch_resolves_note: The fixed `ih264d_parse_fgc()` inserts the missing per-interval `ps_bitstrm->u4_ofst + 8 + 8 < ps_bitstrm->u4_max_ofst` rejection. The fixed original is guarded at the formerly crashing iteration, and the adjacent `insert_zero_stop_before_next_nal_boundary` mutation shows the same protected upper-bound sink still executes cleanly when the predicate is true.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project parser materialization on the crashing path that turns the attacker-controlled NAL bytes into the bit-length boundary state later consumed by SEI bounds checks.

The interval loop starts a lower/upper-bound byte pair without checking that the current bit offset still has room for both 8-bit reads before `ps_bitstrm->u4_max_ofst`; after `ui4_payload_size` is discarded, attacker-controlled component/count fields can therefore carry parsing beyond the valid film-grain payload.

AddressSanitizer sink. `ih264d_get_bits_h264()` performs the actual 4-byte word read for the upper-bound request after the parser has already advanced to the exhausted tail of the heap bitstream buffer.

The upper-bound `ih264d_get_bits_h264(ps_bitstrm, 8)` call executes with the exact second-half offset projected from the same interval pair after the lower-bound read advances `ps_bitstrm->u4_ofst` by 8 bits.
nodes.evidence: On the vulnerable crashing pair, `fgc_pair_guard.expected_upper_offset == fgc_upper_bound_read.upper_read_offset == 2062276`.

edges.evidence: The vulnerable crashing pair records `fgc_pair_guard.expected_upper_offset == fgc_upper_bound_read.upper_read_offset`.
